deck: PRODUCTION-RATE BIDDING, 30% MARGIN FLOORS, AND PROPOSALS SENT WITHIN HOURS OF THE WALKTHROUGH
100-CALL-A-DAY PROSPECTING, PAIN-DECISION-BUDGET QUALIFYING, AND RECURRING CONTRACTS WON ON DEPENDABILITY, NOT THE LOWEST BID
site_ui.lead: Operators who launched under $1,000 and grew to seven figures show how to bid by production rates instead of square footage, turn proposals around within hours of the walkthrough, and win recurring contracts even though roughly 90% of prospects already have a cleaner.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies covering lean launches, first-contract closes, prospecting, bidding formulas, government bids, specialty work, software, OSHA compliance, workforce classification, insurance, and franchise traps. Every claim, metric, pro-tip, and quote carries timestamped inline attribution to the practitioner and video it came from.
chapters: Starting Lean: Founder Playbooks from Zero to Seven Figures
Landing the First Contract: Walkthrough, Proposal, Close, Onboard
Prospecting Engine: Cold Calls, Cold Email, Doors, and Paid Search
Bidding Methods: Production Rates, Square Footage, and Hourly Formulas
Post-Construction Cleaning, Floor Care, and Specialty Add-Ons
Janitorial Software, QR Verification, and Selling with Systems
Bloodborne Pathogens: OSHA Compliance and Spill Cleanup
Franchises, Remote Models, and Ownership Traps
flow: Build a qualified list from Google Maps and call 100 businesses a day; 2,000 calls a month projects 10-20 appointments and 1-2 closes.
Screen every lead on pain, decision, and budget, and offer a complimentary quote to keep on file when the prospect already has a cleaner.
Arrive 20 minutes early, scan for ledge dust, cobwebs, and floor smudges, and laser-measure only cleanable square footage.
Convert footage to labor hours with production rates such as 3,500-4,000 sq ft per hour for offices and hold a 30% margin floor.
Send a forwardable proposal within two to three hours that shows facility understanding, systems, scope, and security procedures.
Set work-order and billing rules up front, price for the employees the account will need, and expand only when current accounts run smoothly.

tagline: Big Money. Small Teams. No Bullshit.
